Commentary.Commentary: Wade and Starc added brisk runs to the total towards the end and as soon as they got out, Steven Smith declared. The Pakistani bowlers were ineffective except Wahab Riaz. They continued with their misery on the field and dropped a few chances. Their confidence will be low at the moment and let's see how they respond with the bat. Join us in a moment for the second innings.

Just when the Pakistani bowlers thought they might be able to expose the inexperienced Aussie middle order, they were pushed back again by a brilliant century from Peter Handscomb. The debutant Cartwright looked promising with the bat too as he put up a good partnership with Handscomb.

That's a massive first innings total posted by Australia! They dominated with the bat right from the word go. They started off with a quickfire century from David Warner which was followed by a daddy hundred by his opening partner, Matthew Renshaw. That just set the tone for the young middle order. It was skipper Steven Smith who had a rare failure with the bat and failed to make his 50th Test memorable.

OUT! What-a-catch! Riaz and substitute fielder Rizwan almost collided but the latter did well to hold on to the catch. Around middle and off, Mitchell Starc tries to heave it across the line but ends up miscuing it high in the air towards mid-wicket. Rizwan comes running in, Riaz also comes running in from deep square leg. No calling whatsoever and the substitute fielder eventually goes for the catch. Riaz stops, tumbles but Rizwan does really well to hold on to the ball. Starc's cameo comes to an end and with that AUSTRALIA HAVE DECLARED ON 538/8!

SIX! Clean as a whistle, says Bill Lawry on air. It's the googly from the Pakistan ODI skipper but Starc reads it well. Stays inside the crease and brings out another mighty slog over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Steven O'Keefe is the new man in!

OUT! In the air.... taken this time! Ali finally gets a wicket! Floated ball around middle and leg, Wade gets down on one knee to slog sweep but gets a big top edge. The ball balloons high in the air towards short fine leg where Babar Azam keeps his eyes on the ball and settles under the skier.
Short and down the leg side, it was asking to be hit. Luckily for Ali, the batsman could only pull it towards deep backward square leg for just a single.
Flatter one around middle and leg, Starc looks to pull but misses and is hit on the pads.
Fuller around middle, Wade hits it down to long on for a single.
Sucker ball! Yorker outside off, MS tries to dig it out but the ball just goes past the off stump to the keeper.
Slower short ball outside off, Starc was winding up for the pull but seeing the lack of pace he leaves it alone.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Starc rides the bounce and pulls it towards mid-wicket for an easy brace.
Sprayed down the leg side, MS looks to tickle it fine down the leg side but fails to do so.
A low full toss on off, Wade jams it towards mid on for a single.
Yorker outside off, Wade tries to dig it out but fails to get any wood on it.

SIX! In the arc for Starc! Tossed up delivery outside off, Mitchell sits down on one knee and absolutely nails the slog sweep as he deposits it over the wide long on fence for half a dozen. Doing the same what he did in his last innings at the G!
Once again on a shorter side, it's pulled towards square leg again for another single.
Short ball around leg, Starc gets down on one knee and pulls it towards deep square leg for a single.
Wade comes forward and clips it towards short fine leg for a single.
Loopy ball around middle, Wade covers the line and defends it down.
Drops it short on middle, it's pulled in front of square for a comfortable couple.
Full outside off, Starc tried to dig it out but was unable to get a contact there.
Mitchell Starc is the new man in!

OUT! What's happened there? That's hit wicket! Fuller delivery outside off, Handscomb goes deep in his crease and guides it towards third man. But there is something we also missed except Sarfraz. The bails were dislodged somehow. He appeals and the decision is referred upstairs. Handscomb starts walking just when Sarfraz appeals. The replays show that in the process of dragging back he did hit the stumps with his bat and one of the bails fell out. That's an end of a very good knock with an unusual dismissal.
Short outside off, Wade flicks it towards square leg for a single.
Handscomb pulls it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Short ball outside off, Wade goes for a pull short which he mistimes and the ball goes towards long on for a triple.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Wade got a bottom edge which nearly rushed back to the stumps.

THAT'S JUST MISSED THE TIMBER! Floated outside off and the ball keeps its line, Handscomb goes for a wild swing on the on side and he totally misjudges it. Luckily the ball just went past the off stump.
On the pads, Wade sweeps it towards short fine leg for a single.

On the stumps, Wade sits down and sweeps it towards square leg for a couple.

Short ball for Wade this time, who pulls it towards square leg for a single.
Short delivery outside off, Peter pulls it towards square leg for a single.
Length ball outside off, Handscomb tries to drive but the ball gets an inside edge which goes down towards fine leg for a couple. 500 runs up for Australia.
Peter walks across and pushes the ball towards the gully fielder.
Full and wide outside off, Peter guides it towards point.
Full and wide outside off, the spin beats the meat of the bat.

On the pads, Wade paddles it towards fine leg for a triple.
2nd Test Century for Peter Handscomb.

FOUR! GLORIOUS! Pitched outside off, Wade walks down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. That was beautiful.

Pakistan on the other hand will be disappointed as they have been ineffective in this session too. They have been totally outplayed by the youngsters from the opposite team. Their bowling has continued to be dismal and they have kept dropping catches as and when possible. They are now staring down the barrel and it will require a monumental effort from them to get back in the match. Join us in a while for the post-lunch session.

So once again a dominant session for the Aussies where they lost just a single wicket and put on nearly hundred runs. They seem to be well on course for a really huge first innings total. Renshaw was the man to depart as he could not reach to his double hundred but Handscomb has continued from where he left last night as he is quite close to his second Test century. The debutant Cartwright has also been impressive with the bat and is amidst a 68-run partnership at the moment with Handscomb.

Goes deep in the crease, shuffles a bit and keeps it out on the leg side.

Advances down the track and milks it down to long on for a single.

Dropped! Ali gives it a loop outside off, turns away a bit after pitching. Cartwright looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge towards first slip where Younis Khan is caught napping. He had his hands on his knees and when the ball came to him he tries to catch but the ball doesn't stick. Goes off his fingers and rolls further. Absolutely poor stuff from the veteran.

Hello and a warm welcome for the coverage of the second day of the SCG Test match between Australia and Pakistan. The visitors will have to make the first hour of morning count if they hope to make it an interesting contest or wish to stay relevant in this match. The hosts on the other hand are riding high on confidence after a brilliant day 1 performance. Renshaw is closing onto his double hundred and Handscomb is looking handsome on the other end as well. Stay with us to find out how the day paves out as the action isn't far away.

The track is a good one for batting and Australia have made full use of the toss they won in the morning. Smith's men are sitting in the driver's seat and would be looking to post a big first innings total. For the tourists, they will have to forget this day sooner than later and come out afresh tomorrow with a better plan. Scalping quick wickets will be the key, but will they be able to do so? Or will we see the home side running away with the game? Join us at 0500 IST to catch all the action from day 2. Until then, it's goodbye and take care. Cheers!

Pakistan tried everything they had but couldn't reap dividends today. It was Riaz who got rid of dangerous looking Warner at the start of the second session and then removed Khawaja as well. Yasir Shah had a tough day once again but will be happy to get a big wicket of skipper Steven Smith. But that was all they managed today. To add to their woes, their fielding once again was below standard with a few chances going down.

What a day for Australia! It's been a day stolen by their openers. If in the morning session, David Warner came out all guns blazing and scored a quickfire century, Matthew Renshaw stood tall till the end and made sure Australia take a firm control of this Test match. He is batting on an unbeaten 167 and along with Peter Handscomb, he is amidst a 121-run stand.

Renshaw has looked solidly on the other end as he has successfully reached to his second Test fifty and is closing on to his debut Test hundred. Smith is out there in the middle supporting him really well in an unorthodox defensive manner in his 50th Test for Australia. Will we see a flurry of wickets in the final session or will the hosts dominate it again? Join us in a while for the final session of the day.

Pakistan have managed to get back into the game a bit. The hosts have managed to put on 98 runs in 27 overs for the second session losing a couple of wickets. Wahab Riaz was the standout performer as he got rid of both Warner and Khawaja. Imran khan was also good with the ball which caused some problems but could not land up with any wicket. The spin duo has been rather ineffective and will have to come to the fore if the visitors wish to cause some trouble to the hosts.

DROPPED! Have Pakistan lost their chance of getting back in the game? Back of a length outside off, Khawaja cuts it fiercely towards gully but that ball went straight to Babar Azam who has dropped a straight forward catch. FIFTY FOR RENSHAW! Tossed up on the stumps, Renshaw has driven it towards long on for a single. Renshaw has reached to his fifty with that. He is continuing from where Warner left.

Outside off, left alone.
Usman Khawaja is in the middle to replace Warner.

OUT! POCKET SIZE DYNAMITE DEPARTS! Back of a length delivery outside off, Warner tries to guide it towards third man but the ball catches the outside edge and goes straight to the keeper. Warner will be unhappy there as he was looking set for a big daddy hundred. The umpire checks for the no ball but much to the delight of Pakistan, this time Riaz was well in line. Sarfraz gets his 100th Test dismissal in the process.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Warner punches it towards covers.
Short into the body, the ball rose more than expected which took Warner by surprise. He still successfully manages to defend it off the upper half of the bat.
On the pads, Renshaw flicks it towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! FIRST ONE AFTER LUNCH! Tossed up on the pads, Renshaw goes for a sweep but gets it off the inside half of the bat which helps the ball go fine towards the leg side for a boundary.

Welcome back for the second session. The players are back out in the middle. Warner and Renshaw will continue from where they left. Yasir Shah will start the proceedings with the ball for Pakistan.
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Are we up for something big from Warner or can the likes of Amir and Riaz reverse swing them back into the game? It should be a fantastic second session. Join us back in a while for the post-lunch session.

Pakistan on the other hand will be pulling their hair out as nothing seems to be going their way and are getting totally outplayed by the hosts. None of the bowlers have managed to put pressure as Warner reached his 18th Test century in no time. They will have to get their act together quickly or else they will be facing a big total on the board.

What a first session of cricket we have witnessed! It's been the Warner show just from the third delivery of the day. He becomes the 4th Australian and 5th batsman overall to score a century in the first session of a Test match. He has just scored boundaries at will and he is looking hungry for more. Renshaw on the other end can play his game without any pressure as Warner is rushing through the scoreboard.
In the corridor outside off, Matthew Renshaw has got nothing to offer on that one. That's the end of an entertaining morning session. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
FOUR! Raiz angles it in but ends up straying on the pads, it's clipped fine down the leg side by Renshaw for a boundary. Easy pickings those.
MR shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length on off, its' blocked well by Renshaw.
18th Test ton for David Warner, 3rd vs Pakistan!

There it is, A TON BEFORE LUNCH! David Warner, please take a bow! 5th overall and 1st Australian to do so in Australia in the first session of the Test. He's one hell of a player! Short and outside off, Warner hits it through backward point. And to add to it there is a misfield in the deep as well which allows him to pick up three. His typical celebration is up next, that famous leap and a punch in the air. The SCG crowd is up on its feet to laud the effort. This is some remarkable feet, and boy, what a way to kick off 2017. Well done, Daveyyyy!
A slip comes out to mid-wicket now...
Back of a length ball on middle, comes up at a nice height, Warner rolls his wrists and pulls it in front of square. The fielder gives it a chase and keeps them down to a couple.
Angles a full ball on off, Matthew Renshaw covers the line and offers a solid defense. A dot ball which means Warner will be on strike on what could be or should be the last over before lunch.
Fuller in the channel outside off, Renshaw once again allows it to go through to the keeper.
A harmless length ball, angling in, MR is happy to let it be.
Touch fuller and outside off, Renshaw defends it down again.
Gets across and bunts it back to Amir.
Short of a length ball on middle, tucked away towards mid-wicket for a single.

Shortish outside off, MR mistimes his cut towards Yasir at point.

Matt defends it from within the crease.
A length ball on off, Warner punches it towards covers. Azhar misfields and that allows him to get a single.

FOUR! What a shot! That's spanked, not even kidding! There was a fielder placed at the boundary but it doesn't matter when Warner hits. Short and outside off, width on offer as well, Davey absolutely nails the cut through cover-point. Yasir in the deep could do nothing about it. Waqar on air says, the hundred is coming (before lunch). Well, he was the one who first said this in the morning.
Third man goes back now...

Angles in a full length delivery on off, Warner stays put and just opens the face of the bat to get it through backward point. He wanted two immediately and some good running between the wickets allows him to come back easily.
Mohammad Amir comes back into the attack as well.

Will he get a ton before lunch? Well, my fellow commentator says, it's just a matter of two or three balls to this man.

Loopy delivery outside off, Warner comes forward and pushes it towards covers for another one.
Around middle, Renshaw drives it down to long on for a single.

FOUR! 100 up for the Aussies! That's a gift which is gleefully accepted by Renshaw. A full toss on the pads, it's whipped away towards mid-wicket. Through the gap and away she goes for a boundary. A fist punch from Warner and this pair is looking really threatening now.
Fuller on middle, Warner's bat turns in his hands as the ball rolls towards mid on and they pick up a single.
Hangs back and defends it gently off the back foot.

He is looking terrific today and surely eyeing for a big one.

It's time to get underway, folks. The players are out in the middle. It shall be David Warner and Matthew Renshaw to open the batting for Australia. Mohammad Amir to have a go with the ball first up. Here we go...

TEAM CHANGES - Both the sides have made a couple of changes and have debutants. For Pakistan, SHARJEEL KHAN (debut) and IMRAN KHAN come in for Sami Aslam and Sohail Khan. For Australia, HILTON CARTRIGHT (debut) and STEPHEN O'KEEFE are brought in place of Nic Maddinson and Jackson Bird.
TOSS - Steven Smith flips the coin. Misbah calls it incorrectly. AUSTRALIA WILL BAT!

Misbah-ul-Haq on the other hand isn't living up to his reputation. He has been going through a lean patch at the moment and he's not the one who allows it to stay with him for long. Pakistan will be really bewailed especially after putting up a fantastic fight in the first Test, folded up under less than two sessions on the flat deck during the Boxing Day Test and thereby saw the series going out of their hands. They will now be playing for pride and the question is will they salvage it? Or will the hosts keep their momentum intact. Let's wait and find out. The toss is coming up in a short while...

Hello and a warm welcome for the 3rd and final Test match between Australia and Pakistan in Sydney. It's the famous Pink Test and just like we saw in MCG, bigger crowd is expected today as well. The hosts will be really pleased with their efforts so far in the series and now will be eyeing for the whitewash. The captain is leading from the front and when that happens, it's a good sign for any team in the world.
